rule: Steam Regular Press (vdf Full_Press) <-> JSM plain binding. Both lanes exact press/release count and order; latency differs (JSM ~2 ms at evdev, Steam ~34 ms pipeline at XI2 raw) but is sub-perception per the human-food doctrine.

Steam Regular+Long_Press (interruptable on) <-> JSM tap'/hold_ pair. Same model both lanes: tap fires on release under threshold, hold fires AT threshold and suppresses tap. Parameterize the boundary per lane (Steam per-binding, inclusive, tick-exact, default 450 ms; JSM global HOLD_PRESS_TIME, +poll slack ~8-16 ms, default 150 ms). Steam->JSM with MULTIPLE distinct Long Press Times collapses to one global value = bounded loss (gotcha X.2, proven both sides). Boundary-edge semantic differences are sub-perception (MOOT). With interruptable 0 Steam fires Regular alongside Long — maps to a DIFFERENT JSM construct than tap/hold; the converter must read the flag.
verdict: exact (single hold-time, interruptable on) / bounded_approximation (multiple hold-times)

rule: Count AND latency delta, both directions. JSM fires the base on the FIRST press (echo) then the double; Steam SUPPRESSES the base and delays every single by exactly DTT from first-down. Window epochs differ: Steam down-to-down, JSM first-release-to-second-down -> window translation: effective JSM window = Steam window - first-press hold time. Steam->JSM gains a base-keystroke echo; JSM->Steam loses the echo and gains +DTT single latency.

Steam Chorded Press <-> JSM chorded press (MOD,BTN syntax). Owner semantics match: chord overrides the owner's base binding. Member behavior: Steam member's own binding LEAKS (verified, by-design); JSM member-leak UNTESTED (verifying trace bound the modifier NONE) — flag member-leak parity as unverified in any conversion where the modifier carries its own binding.

NO Steam counterpart for JSM simultaneous press (Steam has only owner-bound chords). Conversion either direction changes member behavior: JSM SIMPRESS suppresses both members; Steam chord leaks the member. Additionally JSM SIMPRESS itself is degraded (persistent sticky state when a chord member is reused as a lone button). JSM->Steam: convert to chord and name the member-leak change. Steam->JSM: chord maps to JSM chorded press (eq-chord), NOT simpress.

Steam trigger edge(soft)+click(full) <-> JSM ZR/ZRF NO_SKIP — equivalent under STAGED pulls only. Structural delta on instant 0->255: Steam fires full-only, JSM fires soft+full (~3 ms apart). Steam soft threshold is adaptive session state (use RZ=200 for staged probes); JSM threshold is a fixed axis crossing. Soft-pull conversions classify <= bounded_approximation with the adaptive-threshold caveat named.
Steam stick dpad mode <-> JSM LEFT_STICK_MODE=NO_MOUSE + LUP/LDOWN/LLEFT/LRIGHT. Directional keys held while past deadzone, both lanes.
Held-output equivalence is plain key-state hold on both lanes: one down -> held -> one up; no re-send pump to model on either side (Steam Turbo is its own explicit activator setting).

CONVERTER HAZARD RULE (doctrine): any button config mixing Start/Release Press with Long/Double Press is a hazard zone (state-dependent activator loss in Steam — Release eaten universally in the matrix, Double killed under Start+Release co-residency). Classify such inputs <= degraded_approximation with the hazard named; NEVER emit such a combo as converter output (anti-Goodhart: do not engineer configs that depend on replicating a probable Steam bug). This rule absorbs residual uncertainty regardless of further matrix outcomes.

Steam per-binding Long Press Times -> JSM single global HOLD_PRESS_TIME: confirmed bounded loss from BOTH sides (audit gotcha X.2). Pick one global value (e.g. the dominant binding's), name every binding whose effective boundary moves by more than the human tolerance (~10-15 ms is practical equality; 450 vs 603 ms is NOT).
